sources.title: Mathlib, Probability.Kernel.RadonNikodym, Kernel.rnDeriv documentation
sources.locator: Module overview and Kernel.rnDeriv declarations: the jointly measurable derivative construction for finite kernels with a countably generated target; the singular-part identity and the pointwise absolute-continuity criterion.
sources.not_read: Declarations after the jointly measurable derivative and singular-part interfaces were not used. The library item supplies an independent measure-level proof for the probability-kernel specialization.

contents.name: Jointly measurable kernel Radon–Nikodym derivative for countably generated target spaces
contents.reason: The formalized interface corroborates the countably generated-target condition; the item proves the exact probability-kernel, almost-everywhere statement locally.

sources.title: Arnaud Doucet and Adam M. Johansen, A Tutorial on Particle Filtering and Smoothing: Fifteen Years Later
sources.locator: Read §§3.2–3.5, PDF pp. 8–14: path importance-sampling identity and support, SIS incremental-weight recursion, multinomial/residual resampling, generic resample-propagate algorithm, and product estimates.
sources.not_read: Later adaptive-resampling algorithms and application examples were not used. The ESS and immediate-variance caveat at the end of the generic SMC discussion was inspected and is retained only as a scope warning.

contents.name: Path importance-sampling identity, support condition, and product path weight
Sequential proposal and incremental importance-weight recursion
Multinomial and residual offspring-count procedures and their conditional means
Generic resample-propagate algorithm and product estimate of the normalizer
Resampling may add immediate variance; ESS is a weight-imbalance trigger
contents.reason: The algorithm Remarks keep this as a warning and do not turn an ESS trigger into an accuracy, support-coverage, or convergence claim.

sources.title: Simo Särkkä and Lennart Svensson, Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing, 2nd ed.
sources.locator: Read Chapter 11 §§11.2–11.5, printed pp. 231–242: importance-sampling support/weights, SIS recursion, resampling expectation, multinomial and SIR algorithms, bootstrap filter, and sample-impoverishment warning.
sources.not_read: Other chapters, including Chapter 15 on particle smoothing, were not used as support for this pair.

contents.name: Importance-sampling support and target-to-proposal weighting

Resampling preserves the weighted empirical mean and multinomial offspring counts
SIR and bootstrap filter proposal choices
Stratified and systematic resampling alternatives
contents.reason: The controlling BCS-41 design specifically selects multinomial and residual offspring schemes; adding stratified or systematic samplers would expand the approved algorithm inventory.

contents.name: Weight degeneracy, ESS trigger, and sample-impoverishment caveat
contents.reason: The A-page remarks preserve the limit of resampling-based weight diagnostics without claiming a finite-particle accuracy guarantee.

sources.title: Nicolas Chopin, Central Limit Theorem for Sequential Monte Carlo Methods and its Application to Bayesian Inference
sources.locator: Read §§2.1–2.2, PDF pp. 3–7: mutation/correction/selection framework, conditional expected offspring counts, multinomial/residual schemes, and the increasing-path proposal ratio.
sources.not_read: Section 2.3 and later CLT, asymptotic-variance, and application arguments are outside the BCS-41 pair and were not used.

contents.name: Mutation, correction, and selection formulation on increasing path spaces
Multinomial and residual selection schemes with expected count H times normalized weight
Sequential target-to-proposal incremental weight for path extension
General particle-system law of large numbers as particle count grows
contents.reason: The approved BCS-41 claim is exact finite-horizon normalizer unbiasedness; particle-count convergence belongs to the separate BCS-42 error and CLT pair.

contents.name: Systematic selection scheme
contents.reason: Systematic resampling is not among the two offspring procedures approved for BCS-41, which instead proves the multinomial and residual count interface.

sources.title: Arnaud Doucet and Adam M. Johansen, A Tutorial on Particle Filtering and Smoothing: Fifteen Years Later
sources.locator: Read §§3.4–3.5, PDF pp. 13–14: multinomial/residual resampling, generic SMC proposal/update steps, and the normalizer-ratio discussion.
sources.not_read: No finite two-state numerical proposal example is claimed from this source; the item verifies its own finite calculations.

contents.name: Multinomial offspring resampling and weighted empirical target
Sequential proposal weights and normalizer ratio
contents.reason: The example instantiates the source's proposal-weight formula with exact two-state masses and independently checks both resulting normalizer estimates.

sources.locator: Read Chapter 11 §§11.2, 11.4–11.5, printed pp. 231–242: importance-sampling support, resampling, SIR, and the bootstrap filter.
sources.not_read: The book's numerical applications outside the stated two-state model are not imported; all values in these examples are calculated locally.
